Plate-boundary segments: structure feasibility, seismicity style and figure plan (v6.1)

Draft for the Science Advances re-framing (D-B107, PI 2026-11-26 16:05). Built Fri Nov 27 13:26:58 PST 2026; branch analysis/plate-boundaries at e87d4738 (worktree /home/mdenolle/wt_pbplan). Private working page; not peer reviewed. Catalog v6.1 (registered; D-B103, D-B104, D-B105, D-B108): these are the paper numbers (D-B111). Its clustering, Mc maps and fault surfaces are the v6.1 production products; the v6.0 feasibility study is kept at /wd1/mdenolle_data/paper_plan/plate_boundaries_plan.html.

What this page answers. D-B107 asks for a paper on fault-zone structure and seismicity style at the plate boundaries, with velocity structure shown only near faults and only where the model resolves it. Before figures are drawn: which boundaries does model v0.4.2 resolve, how large is the ensemble uncertainty there, how large are the structure contrasts against it, and how do the boundaries differ in seismicity style? Section 5 is the figure plan; draft mock-ups are in sections 4 and 6.

1. Findings

  • Coverage. The rule below sorts 135,317 located tier A-C earthquakes of v6.1 (flagged non-earthquakes and the waveform-review P1 set left out) into 21 segments, 19 of them on plate boundaries. No tomography tile covers the model columns of Axial Seamount, Endeavour or the Explorer segments (n_tiles = 0, DWS = 0), and the JdF plate interior lies at the tile edges (largest P DWS 84 in its columns). So AX, EN, EXR, SOV, JP, EXP have no resolved node; their style metrics stand alone.
  • Resolved for a fault-zone panel (≥ 15 P and ≥ 10 P-and-S nodes within 10 km over ≥ 3 depth layers): BL, MFZ, GP, MTJ, GS, PU, MSH, CAS (plus the non-boundary groups OC and NAPA). Marginal: JR, GR, FA, SIF, IS (Gorda ridge and the northern subduction groups have P nodes only, FA 2 P-and-S nodes; JR has 13 P nodes at 5-7 km). The P-and-S depth span is 9-29 km at Blanco, 21-34 km at the Mendocino fault zone, 21-34 km in the Gorda plate, 9-34 km at the triple junction, 9-25 km in Puget crust and 1-18 km at Mount St Helens.
  • Scale. The finest checkerboard cell that passes near every segment is 40 km, and most near-fault nodes pass the mask on ray sampling alone (DWS ≥ 100): the checkerboard share within 10 km is 28% (P) and 66% (S) at Blanco, 53% at Mount St Helens, 13% in Puget and below 10 % at MFZ, Gorda plate, MTJ and the Gorda slab. The panels can show the structure of the plate-boundary zone on a 40 km scale, not a fault damage zone. Figure captions and the text have to say this.
  • Ensemble 1σ near the faults (median over nodes within 10 km, calibrated): Vp 0.09 km/s at Mount St Helens to 0.28 km/s at Blanco; Vp/Vs 0.020 to 0.055 (raw member spread: the synthetic calibration found Vp/Vs calibrated without inflation, D-B111). The Blanco tile (smoothing 20) has the largest member spread.
  • Contrasts after the circularity control (rule pre-registered 2026-11-27 09:38 PST, commit 6b64abf1, before scoring: a contrast counts only if |Δ| ≥ 2σ of the real ensemble and |Δ| ≥ S95, the 95th percentile of |recovered − truth| over the 100 synthetic members). Of 105 contrasts on resolved and marginal segments, 33 pass 2σ alone (Vp/Vs with the raw σ) and 32 survive both. Dropped by S95: MSH Vp along (-0.061, S95 0.098). The spurious contrasts are small and centred: their sd is about the raw member σ and S95 is a median 0.88 of 2σ, so the synthetic test removes few contrasts. Surviving on the oceanic boundaries: GR Vp near-far -0.22; GR Vp across -0.18; GR Vp along -0.31; MFZ Vp near-far -0.10; MFZ Vs near-far -0.11; GP Vp near-far +0.15; GP Vs across +0.09; at the triple junction and the Gorda slab: MTJ Vp near-far +0.14; MTJ Vp across -0.09; MTJ Vp along -0.44; MTJ Vs near-far +0.14; GS Vp along -0.66; GS Vs near-far -0.18; GS Vs across +0.18; GS Vs along -0.39; on land: PU Vp near-far -0.06; PU Vp across -0.15; PU Vp along +0.10; PU Vp/Vs along +0.02; CAS Vp near-far +0.09; CAS Vp/Vs across +0.02; CAS Vp/Vs along -0.03. Blanco has no surviving contrast (nothing reaches 2σ). No Vp/Vs contrast survives on an oceanic boundary; the Vp/Vs survivors are PU along, CAS across, CAS along (|Δ| 0.016-0.027). The largest values (0.4-0.7 km/s along strike at MTJ and in the Gorda slab) follow the onshore-offshore transition, not a fault zone. The null-truth test (a truth flattened by depth layer near the segments) is approved (D-B112) and not yet scored (section 3).
  • Seismicity style separates the boundary types more clearly than structure does. Swarm share of the events above Mc: Axial 29 %, Mount St Helens 28 %, Blanco 25 %, Gorda ridge 20 %, against ≤ 2.8 % at MFZ, Gorda plate, MTJ and the Gorda slab. Mainshock-aftershock share is highest in the Gorda plate (65 %). b-values range from 0.74 (JdF intraslab) and 0.80 (Axial) to 1.45 (Puget crust). Median depth below the surface: Axial 1.8 km, Blanco 5.5 km, Mount St Helens 6.1 km, Puget 15.7 km, Gorda slab 21.8 km, MTJ 24.0 km, MFZ 25.4 km.
  • Depth against the 7.5 km/s level. The model rarely reaches 8 km/s offshore (MFZ peaks near 7.9 km/s), so the 8 km/s level is resolved in few columns; 7.5 km/s is resolved for 95% of the depth-good Blanco events and 97% at MTJ. Share of events below it: MFZ 75%, Gorda plate 63%, MTJ 54%, Blanco 36%, Gorda slab 23%. Per model column, the bottom of the Gorda-slab seismicity (D90) follows the 7.5 km/s level (ρ = 0.53, p = 0.001 against permuted levels, 67 columns); at Blanco ρ = 0.12, p = 0.010; at MFZ none (p = 0.27). The paper claims this link for the Gorda slab only (D-B111).
  • Swarms against mainshock-aftershock families can be compared on resolved nodes only at Blanco (Vp/Vs: 7 swarm against 27 MA families) and in Puget (7 against 14). Neither differs (smallest p 0.12 over Vp and Vp/Vs), as in the v5.1 analysis. A panel on this would report a null result with few families.

2. Segment rule and segment table

Rule (code workflow/11_paper_plan/pb_common.py, first match wins):

  1. Located events of catalog v6.1 (any tier), first match wins; distances are horizontal.
  2. Traces: spreading axes and the Mendocino transform from pb_axes.py (D-B113: bathymetric axis of the D-B068 merged surface, GMRT where available, where it fits the seismicity better than PB2002; PB2002 elsewhere); subduction trace and the other transforms PB2002.
  3. AX: catalog region Axial. BL: catalog region Blanco. EN: catalog region Endeavour.
  4. MTJ: within 40 km of the PB2002 triple junction (southern end of the JF\NA subduction trace).
  5. MFZ: within 15 km of the PA-JF transform trace, south of 41 N.
  6. Ridges: within 15 km of a PA-JF spreading axis: GR south of 43 N, JR 43-48.35 N, EXR north of 48.35 N.
  7. Explorer region, rest: SOV within 15 km of a transform step, else EXP.
  8. West of the PB2002 subduction trace (oceanic plate): GP south of 43 N, JP north of it.
  9. South of the triple junction latitude (outside MTJ and MFZ): NAPA.
  10. East of the trace, by depth relative to Slab2 (rel = depth - slab): Cascades region: MSH within 25 km of the summit, else CAS. Puget/Georgia and Other onshore: crust (PU, OC) if rel < -10 km or no Slab2. Every other event east of the trace: GS south of 41.5 N; north of it IS if rel >= +5 km, SIF if |rel| < 5 km, FA otherwise (also without Slab2).

Events: located earthquakes of v6.1 (event_flag empty: 3,433 flagged events left out, of them 105 analog_test_signal), tiers A-C, review P1 (Mount St Helens weekly-signal candidates, 116 further tier A-C events) left out. Fault surfaces v1 belong to the segment of most of their fit members at the v6.1 positions (table surface_segments.csv; 124 of 159 surfaces have ≥ 80 % of their members in one segment). Threshold sensitivity is in section 7.

Plate-boundary axes (D-B113)

PB2002 places the southern Gorda Ridge 10-20 km west of its axial valley and of its seismicity, so the 15 km buffer missed it and its events fell in the Gorda plate group. The spreading axes and the Mendocino transform are re-picked from the bathymetry (code pb_axes.py): the D-B068 merged solid surface (/wd1/mdenolle_data/reloc_v5/topo/topo_15s_cons_merged.bin; GMRT multibeam where available, GMT earth_relief 01m elsewhere), profiles across the PB2002 trace every 2 km, two candidates per profile (axial valley: deepest point, 1.5 km smoothing, 10 km median filter; axial high: highest point within 15 km, 4 km smoothing, 18 km median filter); for the Mendocino transform the crest of the Mendocino Ridge and the base of its north-facing slope. PB2002 is replaced in a section only where its 15 km buffer misses at least 10 % of the nearby tier A-C earthquakes and a bathymetric candidate keeps at least 10 percentage points more of them within 15 km without a larger median distance. The candidates come from the bathymetry; the seismicity only chooses among them. Chosen: the axial valley for the southern Gorda Ridge (40.45-41.6 N) and the axial high for the Juan de Fuca section 46.4-47.7 N; PB2002 elsewhere. The Mendocino transform keeps PB2002: its seismicity lies 8-12 km north of the trace, but the buffer already holds 66 % of the nearby events and the base-of-slope pick only 71 %; the rest are Gorda-plate lineaments north of the transform. Blanco events are assigned by the catalog region, so the Blanco trace does not enter the rule; Sovanco and the Explorer ridge keep PB2002 (unconstrained locations). Buffer unchanged (15 km). 1,280 tier A-C earthquakes change segment.

PB2002 (cyan) and the chosen bathymetric axes (yellow) on the shaded merged surface, with the tier A-C earthquakes.

3. Structure feasibility

Model v0.4.2 on its node grid (0.125° x 0.1°, about 10 x 11 km; depth nodes 2-6 km apart above 30 km). Masks as used so far: rock and (checkerboard-resolved or DWS ≥ 100), P for Vp, S for Vs, both for Vp/Vs; nodes whose Vs was reverted to the reference (D-B051) are left out of the S mask. Distance of a node: 3-D distance to the nearest point of the segment's fault surfaces (1 km mesh) or of its seismicity (depth-good events where there are ≥ 50, else tier A-C). Ensemble 1σ: v0.4.2+ens.100 Vp_std (x 1.50) and Vs_std (x 1.35) as stored; Vp/Vs: the raw member std (factor 1.0, D-B111). Class: resolved ≥ 15 P and ≥ 10 P-and-S nodes within 10 km over ≥ 3 depth layers; marginal ≥ 5 P nodes within 10 km; else not resolved. Spans list depth layers with ≥ 3 nodes.

Contrasts against the ensemble

Depth-matched contrasts (per depth layer, weighted by the smaller node count): near-far = nodes within 5 km minus nodes 10-20 km away; across = the two sides of the segment's strike line (PCA of its epicentres; nodes within 3 km of the line left out; + = left of the strike direction); along = the third of the nodes within 10 km at the strike-azimuth end (strike 0-180°, segment_axes.csv) minus the third at the other end. σ of Δ: the same contrast in each of the 100 members, std x calibration factor. "members same sign" = share of members whose contrast has the sign of the v0.4.2 value.

Circularity control (synthetic ensemble, D-B111)

Rule, pre-registered in data/paper_plan/plate_boundaries/RESUME.md at Fri Nov 27 09:38:33 PST 2026 (commit 6b64abf1, pushed before any synthetic contrast was computed): a contrast counts only if |Δ_real| ≥ 2σ_ens (Vp x1.50, Vs x1.35, Vp/Vs x1.00) and |Δ_real| ≥ S95, where S95 is the 95th percentile of |Δ_rec,i − Δ_truth| over the synthetic members; fewer than 50 members with a value means not testable.

Synthetic set: /wd1/mdenolle_data/tomo_v1/ensemble_v0.4.2/synth, one truth (v0.4.2 tomography x (1 + f), 3 % random field, 30 km / 8 km correlation, truth hypocentres drawn about v4-NLL3D), synthetic data on the real event-station geometry and pick list, 100 members s000-s099 inverted from their own start draws, and five noise-floor clones of s000. The same node sets and depth matching as the real contrasts; truth and members compared before the D-B073 node rule. Spurious contrast = recovered − truth: it holds what ray sampling, the events' trade-offs and the regularisation do to a contrast that is in the truth. All 105 contrasts were testable.

Null truth. Every member of the calibration set inverts data from the same truth, which carries the v0.4.2 contrasts, so that set cannot show whether coverage creates a contrast from nothing. A null-truth ensemble (D-B112: depth-layer means within 45 km of the segments, about 20 members, root /wd1/mdenolle_data/tomo_v1/ensemble_v0.4.2_null) is approved; its rule is pre-registered in RESUME.md before scoring. Not scored yet.

Real contrasts with ±2σ of the real ensemble and ±S95 of the synthetic spurious contrasts (grey). Filled = survives the pre-registered rule. Colours by segment type. Draft.

4. Seismicity-style metrics

Mc: maximum curvature + 0.2 on the segment's tier A-C magnitudes (v6.1 M: converged magnitudes on the v6.1 hypocentres, D-B105); b: Aki-Utsu for continuous magnitudes above Mc; both re-estimated in 500 event bootstrap draws (95 % intervals). "Mc map": event-weighted median of the v6.1 Mc map cells (flagged events excluded). Clustering shares: v6.1 nearest-neighbour clustering, events in its analysis set (above the regional Mc of that run), with a bootstrap over units (one background event or one whole family).

Seismicity-style fingerprint of the plate-boundary segments (mock-up of main figure 2). Label: segment code and structure class (r resolved, m marginal, n not resolved). Draft.

Depth and geometry

bsf = depth below the solid surface (ground or seafloor), depth-good events only (tier A-C, depth_quality ok, not floor-limited, far-only or deep-pass). For segments without depth-good events the raw median is given in the "unconstrained" column and should not be used. 7.5 and 8 km/s levels: depth of the first Vp crossing in the event's model column between two P-resolved nodes; "members p05/p95" = the share recomputed with each member's level (raw spread). Fault-surface columns: v1 surfaces of the segment (dip weighted by member count; seismogenic width = 2-98 % depth range of depth-ok members).

Temporal character

Events ≥ the segment Mc over the whole period. COV = coefficient of variation of inter-event times (1 for a Poisson process); burstiness = (σ − μ)/(σ + μ). The network changed with the OBS deployments (2011-2015) and Axial enters tier A-C only from 2013-09, so rates and burstiness compare segments only roughly.

Mount St Helens swarm share, v6.0 to v6.1, family by family

Each v6.0 swarm family with events in the Mount St Helens analysis set, the v6.1 families its events fall in, and what became of each event (code pb_swarm_change.py). The share falls from 38 % (107 of 282 events) to 28 % (69 of 243). Without the 131 analog_test_signal events the v6.0 share is still 38 % (103 of 268): the flags remove 14 analysis events, 4 of them swarm events. Of the 107 v6.0 swarm events, 60 stay swarm events; 13 drop to tier D, 4 carry the analog flag, 2 are not located, 1 falls below Mc; 11 move into multiplets, 11 into a mainshock-aftershock family and 5 into the background. The largest single change is family 144 (2011-01-28, Mmax 3.96): its v6.1 successor 142 no longer meets the chain criterion and is typed mainshock-aftershock. Families 1434 (2014-11) and 1987 (2015-08) break into multiplets. The drop is a reclassification of small and medium families, not the analog flags; this is the family instability D-B111 names.

5. Figure plan

Six main figures, each a set of small multiples with segments on a shared axis and one colour or marker per boundary type (ridge, transform, intraplate, triple junction, subduction, crustal, arc). Velocity appears only in figures 4 and 5 and only on resolved nodes near the segments. All on catalog v6.1 and model v0.4.2.

6. Mock-up: fault-normal sections, Blanco and Mendocino fault zone

Model v0.4.2 on resolved nodes in 5 km bins of fault-normal distance (≥ 2 nodes per bin), stacked along 355 km (Blanco) and 298 km (MFZ) of the PB2002 transform trace and centred on the seismicity (trace offset -5.3 km and +7.9 km). Rows: Vp, its 1σ (x1.50), Vp/Vs (P and S mask), its 1σ (raw, D-B111). Dots: depth-good tier A-C events of the segment. Dashed: 7.5 km/s. Draft.

What the mock-up shows: within 10 km of the Blanco faults and seismicity the resolved layers span 3-40 km for Vp and 9-29 km for Vp/Vs and the seismicity sits in them; at MFZ 15-40 km (P) and 21-34 km (P and S), with 75% of the seismicity below the 7.5 km/s level. Median Vp 1σ: Blanco 0.28 km/s, MFZ 0.21 km/s. Structure within ±10 km of the faults is near the node spacing.

7. Caveats

  • Catalog v6.1 limits (README, D-B110): Axial tier A-B events 73 % within 2 km of the seafloor (target 85 %; near-surface Vp/Vs of the model, fix in v6.2); flagged events fed the station terms; 129 candidate clock epochs and the location-review verdicts wait for v6.2; no coherence relocation at Mendocino. Paper stance (D-B111): deep events under Mount St Helens are not interpreted; family-level claims only for large sequences; the seismicity-bottom link to the 7.5 km/s level is claimed for the Gorda slab only.
  • No structure for Axial, Endeavour and Explorer (outside every tomography tile) or the JdF plate interior (tile edges, DWS below 100).
  • Resolution: 40 km checkerboard cells and a 10 km node grid. Most nodes near the faults pass the mask on DWS ≥ 100 only, which shows ray sampling, not resolution. Ray coverage follows the seismicity, so velocity near events can be biased in the same place the events are. The synthetic-ensemble control (section 3) bounds the error of contrasts present in the truth; a null-truth synthetic, which would show contrasts created from nothing, has not been run.
  • Uncertainty: the ensemble 1σ for Vp and Vs is calibrated (x 1.50, x 1.35; D-B099); Vp/Vs uses the raw spread (calibrated without inflation, D-B111). The member spread does not include smoothing bias from limited resolution; the synthetic recovery ratios of the surviving contrasts (median 1.01, 10-90 % 0.82-1.36) give its size for this truth.
  • Depths: the ridges other than Axial, Explorer and the JdF plate have depth_quality unconstrained; Gorda events are mostly biased_deep (454 depth-good of 4,957 Gorda-plate events); Blanco depth-good events have median σz 4.8 km and a deep tail against Lange et al. (2026). Depth rows are marked fair or none accordingly.
  • Segment rule: PB2002 traces are approximate (MFZ seismicity lies +8 km and Blanco -5 km from the trace, + north); the thresholds (MTJ radius, axis half-width, 41.5 N, ±5 km about Slab2) are choices. MTJ changes from 6,703 to 14,010 events between radii of 30 and 50 km; the interface-zone group SIF from 831 to 1,823 between ±3 and ±8 km.
  • Fault surfaces v1 refit on v6.1; 51 of 137 non-strand surfaces are marked stable under detection reruns. Dips and widths here are descriptive.
  • Clustering: the v6.1 run used its own regional Mc (AX, EN, BL, GO, MT, WA, OR, PU, ON), not the segment Mc. Positions, magnitudes and tiers of its event table match the catalog file read here (checked when this page was built). Bootstrap intervals ignore correlation in time.
  • Temporal metrics depend on network changes; they are rough comparisons only.
